2 Measurement.question:
Task 1: On a piece of paper, sketch a diagram of the silo described below. Label the radius, the cylinder height, and the cone height with their respective dimensions.

Task 2: A farm silo is shaped like a composite solid consisting of a cylinder topped by a cone. The silo has a radius of {r} m. The cylindrical section has a height of {h_cyl} m, and the conical roof section has a height of {h_cone} m.

1. Calculate the total external surface area that needs to be painted (excluding the ground base and the shared internal boundary).
2. Calculate the total internal volume of the silo.

Provide your answers in both exact terms of \(\pi\) and as a decimal approximation rounded to the nearest tenth.
2 Measurement.answer:
Expected Student Sketch Reference:



Step-by-Step Solution Breakdown:

Step 1: Find the Cone Slant Height (\(\ell\))
Using the Pythagorean theorem: \(\ell = \sqrt{r^2 + h_{\text{cone}}^2}\)
\(\ell = \sqrt{{r}^2 + {h_cone}^2} = \sqrt{{slant_sq}} \approx {slant_str}\text{ m}\)

Step 2: Calculate the Painted Surface Area (Lateral Areas Only)
• Cylinder Lateral Area: \(2\pi rh_{\text{cyl}} = 2\pi({r})({h_cyl}) = {cyl_area_coeff}\pi\)
• Cone Lateral Area: \(\pi r\ell = \pi({r})({slant_str}) = {cone_area_coeff}\pi\)
• Total Area (Exact): \(({cyl_area_coeff} + {cone_area_coeff})\pi = {pi_area_coeff}\pi\text{ m}^2\)
• Total Area (Decimal): \({pi_area_coeff} \times 3.14159... = \mathbf{{dec_area}\text{ m}^2}\)

Step 3: Calculate the Total Volume
• Cylinder Volume: \(\pi r^2 h_{\text{cyl}} = \pi({r}^2)({h_cyl}) = {cyl_vol_coeff}\pi\)
• Cone Volume: \(\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h_{\text{cone}} = \frac{1}{3}\pi({r}^2)({h_cone}) = {cone_vol_coeff}\pi\)
• Total Volume (Exact): \(({cyl_vol_coeff} + {cone_vol_coeff})\pi = {pi_vol_coeff}\pi\text{ m}^3\)
• Total Volume (Decimal): \({pi_vol_coeff} \times 3.14159... = \mathbf{{dec_vol}\text{ m}^3}\)

2 Measurement.question:
Task 1: On a piece of paper, sketch a diagram of the decorative wooden fence post described below. Label the base width, the main prism height, and the top pyramid height with their respective dimensions.

Task 2: A wooden fence post is shaped like a composite solid consisting of a square prism topped by a square-based pyramid cap. The post has a square base side width of {w} cm. The main cylindrical-prism section has a height of {h_prism} cm, and the decorative pyramid roof cap has a height of {h_pyramid} cm.

1. Calculate the total external surface area that needs to be painted or stained (excluding the bottom base flat on the ground and the shared internal boundary interface).
2. Calculate the total volume of wood required to construct the fence post.

Provide your answers as decimal values rounded to the nearest tenth. Do not include π in your calculations since this is a flat-faced polygon solid.
2 Measurement.answer:
Expected Student Sketch Reference:



Step-by-Step Solution Breakdown:

Step 1: Find the Face Slant Height (\(\ell\)) of the Pyramid
The distance from the center of the base to the edge is half the width: \({w} / 2 = {half_w}\text{ cm}\).
Using the Pythagorean theorem: \(\ell = \sqrt{(\frac{w}{2})^2 + h_{\text{pyramid}}^2}\)
\(\ell = \sqrt{{half_w}^2 + {h_pyramid}^2} = \sqrt{{slant_sq}} \approx {slant_str}\text{ cm}\)

Step 2: Calculate the Painted Surface Area (Exposed Faces Only)
• Prism Lateral Area (4 vertical rectangular faces): \(4 \times w \times h_{\text{prism}} = 4 \times {w} \times {h_prism} = {prism_area}\text{ cm}^2\)
• Pyramid Lateral Area (4 triangular faces): \(4 \times (\frac{1}{2} \times w \times \ell) = 2 \times {w} \times {slant_str} \approx {pyramid_area}\text{ cm}^2\)
• Total Painted Area: \({prism_area} + {pyramid_area} = \mathbf{{total_area}\text{ cm}^2}\br>
Step 3: Calculate the Total Wood Volume
• Prism Volume: \(w^2 \times h_{\text{prism}} = {w}^2 \times {h_prism} = {prism_vol}\text{ cm}^3\)
• Pyramid Volume: \(\frac{1}{3} \times w^2 \times h_{\text{pyramid}} = \frac{1}{3} \times {w}^2 \times {h_pyramid} \approx {pyramid_vol}\text{ cm}^3\)
• Total Volume: \({prism_vol} + {pyramid_vol} = \mathbf{{total_vol}\text{ cm}^3}\)

2 Angles and Geometric Figures.question:
Use the geometric diagram below to answer the following questions.
{lines_svg}

A. Write the name of the angle formed by ray \( \overrightarrow{{v}{p1}} \) and ray \( \overrightarrow{{v}{p6}} \).
B. Write two vertical angles shown in the diagram and state their relationship.
C. Write two angles that form a linear pair.
D. Write two opposite rays.
2 Angles and Geometric Figures.answer:
Refer to the diagram for verification:
{lines_svg}

A. The angle formed by ray \( \overrightarrow{{v}{p1}} \) and ray \( \overrightarrow{{v}{p6}} \) is named \( \angle {p1}{v}{p6} \) (or \( \angle {p6}{v}{p1} \)).

B. Vertical angles are opposite each other across an intersection and are equal in measure. Example pairs include \( \angle {p1}{v}{p3} \) and \( \angle {p4}{v}{p6} \), where \( \angle {p1}{v}{p3} = \angle {p4}{v}{p6} \). (Other valid pairs include \( \angle {p1}{v}{p2} \) and \( \angle {p4}{v}{p5} \), or \( \angle {p3}{v}{p5} \) and \( \angle {p2}{v}{p6} \)).

C. A linear pair consists of adjacent angles whose non-common sides form a straight line. An example pair is \( \angle {p1}{v}{p3} \) and \( \angle {p3}{v}{p4} \). (Any two adjacent angles along a straight line, such as \( \angle {p1}{v}{p2} \) and \( \angle {p2}{v}{p4} \), are correct).

D. Opposite rays share a common endpoint and extend in completely opposite directions along the same line. Valid pairs from this diagram are: \( \overrightarrow{{v}{p1}} \) and \( \overrightarrow{{v}{p4}} \), \( \overrightarrow{{v}{p2}} \) and \( \overrightarrow{{v}{p5}} \) or \( \overrightarrow{{v}{p3}} \) and \( \overrightarrow{{v}{p6}} \).

2 Angles and Geometric Figures.question:
Use the geometric diagram below to solve the problem.
{bisector_svg}

In the figure, \( \overrightarrow{ED} \) and \( \overrightarrow{EA} \) are opposite rays, and \( \overrightarrow{EB} \) bisects \( \angle AEC \).

If \( m\angle AEC = {angle_aec}^\circ \) and \( m\angle AEB = {k}x^\circ \), then what is the value of \( x \)?
2 Angles and Geometric Figures.answer:
Refer to the diagram for verification:
{bisector_svg}

Since \( \overrightarrow{EB} \) bisects \( \angle AEC \), it divides the angle into two equal halves. Therefore, the measure of \( \angle AEB \) is exactly half the measure of \( \angle AEC \):
\( m\angle AEB = \frac{m\angle AEC}{2} \)
\( m\angle AEB = \frac{{angle_aec}^\circ}{2} = {angle_aeb}^\circ \)

We are given that \( m\angle AEB = {k}x^\circ \). Set up the equation to solve for \( x \):
\( {k}x = {angle_aeb} \)
\( x = \frac{{angle_aeb}}{{k}} \)
\( x = {x_val} \)

2 Angles and Geometric Figures.question:
Use the geometric diagram below to solve the problem.
{question_svg}

In the figure, \( \angle {pD}{v}{pC} \) and \( \angle {pA}{v}{pB} \) are complementary and congruent. Mark the two angles as congruent on the diagram and list the value of each. (drawing not to scale)
2 Angles and Geometric Figures.answer:
Here is the diagram with the matching congruence tick marks indicating that the two angles are equal:
{answer_svg}

Step 1: Apply definitions
• Complementary angles add up to exactly \( 90^\circ \).
• Congruent angles have completely equal measures, so \( m\angle {pD}{v}{pC} = m\angle {pA}{v}{pB} \).

Step 2: Calculate the values
Let the measure of each angle be represented by \( x \):
\( x + x = 90^\circ \)
\( 2x = 90^\circ \)
\( x = 45^\circ \)

Therefore, the value of each angle is:
• \( m\angle {pD}{v}{pC} = 45^\circ \)
• \( m\angle {pA}{v}{pB} = 45^\circ \)

2 Angles and Geometric Figures.objective: Find the measure of supplementary angles
2 Angles and Geometric Figures.question: Two angles are supplementary. The measure of the larger angle is {n} times greater than the measure of the smaller angle. What is the measure of the smaller angle?
2 Angles and Geometric Figures.answer: Let the measure of the smaller angle be \( x \). Since the angles are supplementary, their sum is \( 180^\circ \). The larger angle is \( {n}x \). Set up the equation: \( x + {n}x = 180 \) or \( \left({n} + 1\right)x = 180 \). Solving for \( x \) gives the smaller angle: \( x = {smaller_angle}^\circ \) (and the larger angle is \( {larger_angle}^\circ \)).

2 Angles and Geometric Figures.objective: Find the measure of complimentary angles
2 Angles and Geometric Figures.question: Two angles are complimentary. The measure of the larger angle is {n} times greater than the measure of the smaller angle. What is the measure of the smaller angle?
2 Angles and Geometric Figures.answer: Let the measure of the smaller angle be \( x \). Since the angles are complimenary, their sum is \( 90^\circ \). The larger angle is \( {n}x \). Set up the equation: \( x + {n}x = 90 \) or \( \left({n} + 1\right)x = 90 \). Solving for \( x \) gives the smaller angle: \( x = {smaller_angle}^\circ \) (and the larger angle is \( {larger_angle}^\circ \)).

2 Angles and Geometric Figures.question:
A circle is drawn on a coordinate plane. The center of the circle is at point C({h}, {k}), and a point on the outer edge of the circle is located at P({p_x}, {p_y}).

Find the **circumference** and the **area** of the circle. For each measurement, provide both the exact answer in terms of pi and a decimal approximation rounded to four significant figures.
2 Angles and Geometric Figures.answer:
1. **Find the radius (r):** Use the distance formula between center C({h}, {k}) and point P({p_x}, {p_y}).
r = √( {p_x} - {h} )² + ( {p_y} - {k} )²
r = √{r_squared}
r = {r}

2. **Calculate Circumference:**
- Exact: C = 2 * pi * r = 2 * pi * {r} = {circumference_coefficient}pi
- Decimal Approximation: {circumference_approx} (to four significant figures)

3. **Calculate Area:**
- Exact: A = pi * r² = pi * ({r})² = {r_squared}pi
- Decimal Approximation: {area_approx} (to four significant figures).

2 Angles and Geometric Figures.objective: Calculate the Perimeter and Area of a Tilted Rectangle on a Coordinate Plane
2 Angles and Geometric Figures.question:
A rectangle has vertices at the following coordinates on a coordinate plane:
A({a_x}, {a_y}), B({b_x}, {b_y}), C({c_x}, {c_y}), and D({d_x}, {d_y}).

Find the **perimeter** and the **area** of rectangle ABCD.
2 Angles and Geometric Figures.answer:
1. **Find Side Length AB:** Use the distance formula between A({a_x}, {a_y}) and B({b_x}, {b_y}).
AB = √( {b_x} - {a_x} )² + ( {b_y} - {a_y} )²
AB = √( {v1_x} )² + ( {v1_y} )²
AB = √{v1_x_sq} + {v1_y_sq}
AB = √{v1_sum}
AB = {str_side1}

2. **Find Side Length AD:** Use the distance formula between A({a_x}, {a_y}) and D({d_x}, {d_y}).
AD = √( {d_x} - {a_x} )² + ( {d_y} - {a_y} )²
AD = √( {v2_x} )² + ( {v2_y} )²
AD = √{v2_x_sq} + {v2_y_sq}
AD = √{v2_sum}
AD = {str_side2}

3. **Calculate Perimeter:**
P = 2 * (AB + AD)
P = 2 * ({str_side1} + {str_side2})
P = {str_perimeter}

4. **Calculate Area:**
A = AB * AD
A = {str_side1} * {str_side2}
A = {str_area}

2 Angles and Geometric Figures.objective: Rotate a Triangle About the Origin by 90, 180, or 270 Degrees and Sketch
2 Angles and Geometric Figures.question:
Triangle ABC has vertices at the following coordinates on a coordinate plane:
A({a_x}, {a_y}), B({b_x}, {b_y}), and C({c_x}, {c_y}).

1. **Sketch** the pre-image triangle ABC on a coordinate grid.
2. Find the coordinates of the image triangle A'B'C' after a **{angle}° counterclockwise** rotation about the origin.
3. **Sketch** the resulting image triangle A'B'C' on the same coordinate grid.
2 Angles and Geometric Figures.answer:
1. Sketch the Pre-Image: Plot points A({a_x}, {a_y}), B({b_x}, {b_y}), and C({c_x}, {c_y}) on your coordinate grid and connect them to form triangle ABC.

2. Apply the Rotation Rule:
For a counterclockwise rotation about the origin:
- A 90° rotation follows the rule (x, y) -> (-y, x).
- A 180° rotation follows the rule (x, y) -> (-x, -y).
- A 270° rotation follows the rule (x, y) -> (y, -x).

3. Calculate Image Coordinates:
- Vertex A: A({a_x}, {a_y}) -> A'({a_prime_x}, {a_prime_y})
- Vertex B: B({b_x}, {b_y}) -> B'({b_prime_x}, {b_prime_y})
- Vertex C: C({c_x}, {c_y}) -> C'({c_prime_x}, {c_prime_y})

4. Sketch the Image: Plot points A'({a_prime_x}, {a_prime_y}), B'({b_prime_x}, {b_prime_y}), and C'({c_prime_x}, {c_prime_y}) on your grid and connect them to form the rotated triangle A'B'C'.

**Final Coordinates:**
A'({a_prime_x}, {a_prime_y}), B'({b_prime_x}, {b_prime_y}), and C'({c_prime_x}, {c_prime_y}).

2 Angles and Geometric Figures.question:
Task 1: On a piece of paper, sketch a 3D diagram of the toy chest described below. Label its length, width, and height with their respective dimensions.

Task 2: A wooden children's toy chest is constructed in the shape of a perfect rectangular prism. The chest measures {l} cm in length, {w} cm in width, and stands {h} cm tall.

1. Calculate the total external surface area of the entire closed wooden chest.
2. Calculate the total internal volumetric storage capacity of the chest.

Provide your final surface area in square centimeters (cm²) and volume in cubic centimeters (cm³).
2 Angles and Geometric Figures.answer:
Expected Student Sketch: The sketch should depict a 3D rectangular prism (box structure). The longest horizontal front edge must be labeled as {l} cm, the depth/receding horizontal edge labeled as {w} cm, and the vertical edge labeled as {h} cm.



Mathematical Steps & Calculations:

1. Total External Surface Area:
• Formula: \(A = 2(lw + lh + wh)\)
• Top & Bottom Faces: \(2 \cdot ({l} \cdot {w}) = 2 \cdot {base_area} = \) \(2 \cdot {base_area}\) cm²
• Front & Back Faces: \(2 \cdot ({l} \cdot {h}) = \) {front_back_area} cm²
• Left & Right Side Faces: \(2 \cdot ({w} \cdot {h}) = \) {side_area} cm²
• Total Surface Area: {total_area} cm²

2. Total Volumetric Capacity:
• Formula: \(V = l \cdot w \cdot h\)
• Volume Calculation: \({l} \cdot {w} \cdot {h}\)
• Total Volume: {total_vol} cm³

2 Angles and Geometric Figures.question:
Task 1: On a piece of paper, sketch a diagram of the water tank described below. Label the radius and the height with their respective dimensions.

Task 2: An industrial water tank is shaped like a perfect cylinder. The tank has a base radius of {r} m and a vertical height of {h} m.

1. Calculate the total external surface area of the water tank (including both flat circular bases).
2. Calculate the total internal volumetric capacity of the water tank.

Provide your answers in both exact terms of \(\pi\) and as a decimal approximation rounded to the nearest tenth.
2 Angles and Geometric Figures.answer:
Expected Student Sketch: The sketch should depict a vertical cylinder with a flat circular top and bottom. A dashed or solid radius line on one of the circular faces should be labeled as {r} m, and the vertical height connecting the two bases should be labeled as {h} m.



Mathematical Steps & Calculations:

1. Total External Surface Area:
• Formula: \(A = 2\pi r^2 + 2\pi rh\)
• Base Area Component: \(2 \cdot \pi \cdot {r}^2 = {base_area_coeff}\pi\) m² (for both bases)
• Lateral Area Component: \(2 \cdot \pi \cdot {r} \cdot {h} = {lateral_area_coeff}\pi\) m²
• Total Surface Area (Exact): {total_area_coeff}\(\pi\) m²
• Total Surface Area (Decimal): {dec_area} m²

2. Total Volumetric Capacity:
• Formula: \(V = \pi r^2 h\)
• Volume Calculation: \(\pi \cdot {r}^2 \cdot {h} = {vol_coeff}\pi\)
• Total Volume (Exact): {vol_coeff}\(\pi\) m³
• Total Volume (Decimal): {dec_vol} m³

2 Angles and Geometric Figures.question:
Task 1: On a piece of paper, sketch a diagram of the silo described below. Label the radius, the cylinder height, and the cone height with their respective dimensions.

Task 2: A farm silo is shaped like a composite solid consisting of a cylinder topped by a cone. The silo has a radius of {r} m. The cylindrical section has a height of {h_cyl} m, and the conical roof section has a height of {h_cone} m.

1. Calculate the total external surface area that needs to be painted (excluding the ground base and the shared internal boundary).
2. Calculate the total internal volume of the silo.

Provide your answers in both exact terms of \(\pi\) and as a decimal approximation rounded to the nearest tenth.
2 Angles and Geometric Figures.answer:
Expected Student Sketch Reference:



Step-by-Step Solution Breakdown:

Step 1: Find the Cone Slant Height (\(\ell\))
Using the Pythagorean theorem: \(\ell = \sqrt{r^2 + h_{\text{cone}}^2}\)
\(\ell = \sqrt{{r}^2 + {h_cone}^2} = \sqrt{{slant_sq}} \approx {slant_str}\text{ m}\)

Step 2: Calculate the Painted Surface Area (Lateral Areas Only)

Task 1: On a piece of paper, sketch a diagram of the decorative wooden fence post described below. Label the base width, the main prism height, and the top pyramid height with their respective dimensions.

1. Calculate the total external surface area that needs to be painted or stained (excluding the bottom base flat on the ground and the shared internal boundary interface).

Step-by-Step Solution Breakdown:

Step 1: Find the Face Slant Height (\(\ell\)) of the Pyramid
The distance from the center of the base to the edge is half the width: \({w} / 2 = {half_w}\text{ cm}\).
Using the Pythagorean theorem: \(\ell = \sqrt{(\frac{w}{2})^2 + h_{\text{pyramid}}^2}\)
\(\ell = \sqrt{{half_w}^2 + {h_pyramid}^2} = \sqrt{{slant_sq}} \approx {slant_str}\text{ cm}\)

Step 2: Calculate the Painted Surface Area (Exposed Faces Only)
• Prism Lateral Area (4 vertical rectangular faces): \(4 \times w \times h_{\text{prism}} = 4 \times {w} \times {h_prism} = {prism_area}\text{ cm}^2\)
• Pyramid Lateral Area (4 triangular faces): \(4 \times (\frac{1}{2} \times w \times \ell) = 2 \times {w} \times {slant_str} \approx {pyramid_area}\text{ cm}^2\)
• Total Painted Area: \({prism_area} + {pyramid_area} = \mathbf{{total_area}\text{ cm}^2}\br>
Step 3: Calculate the Total Wood Volume
• Prism Volume: \(w^2 \times h_{\text{prism}} = {w}^2 \times {h_prism} = {prism_vol}\text{ cm}^3\)
• Pyramid Volume: \(\frac{1}{3} \times w^2 \times h_{\text{pyramid}} = \frac{1}{3} \times {w}^2 \times {h_pyramid} \approx {pyramid_vol}\text{ cm}^3\)
• Total Volume: \({prism_vol} + {pyramid_vol} = \mathbf{{total_vol}\text{ cm}^3}\)

3 Logical Arguments and Line Relationshi.question:
Sketch a geometric diagram according to the following: Points {ptA}, {ptB}, and {ptD} form a straight angle line with \( \overrightarrow{{ptB}{ptC}} \) extending upward:



Statements:
\( p \): \( \angle {ptA}{ptB}{ptC} \) and \( \angle {ptC}{ptB}{ptD} \) are complementary.
\( q \): \( \angle {ptA}{ptB}{ptC} \) and \( \angle {ptC}{ptB}{ptD} \) are vertical angles.
\( r \): \( \overline{{ptA}{ptB}} \cong \overline{{ptB}{ptD}} \)

Write out the compound statement for the conjunction \( \sim p \wedge \sim q \) in words, determine its final truth value, and explain your reasoning fully.
3 Logical Arguments and Line Relationshi.answer:
Here is the complete logical breakdown and step-by-step evaluation for the compound logic statement:

Step 1: Write the compound statement in words.
The symbol \( \sim \) represents a negation ("not"), and the symbol \( \wedge \) represents a conjunction ("and"). Translating \( \sim p \wedge \sim q \) gives:
"\( \angle {ptA}{ptB}{ptC} \) and \( \angle {ptC}{ptB}{ptD} \) are NOT complementary, AND \( \angle {ptA}{ptB}{ptC} \) and \( \angle {ptC}{ptB}{ptD} \) are NOT vertical angles."

Step 2: Evaluate the truth value of individual statement \( p \) and its negation \( \sim p \).
Complementary angles must add up to exactly \( 90^\circ \). Because points \( {ptA} \), \( {ptB} \), and \( {ptD} \) form a straight angle line, they are a linear pair and must sum to exactly \( 180^\circ \) (supplementary) by the Linear Pair Postulate. Therefore, statement \( p \) is false, making its negation \( \sim p \) TRUE.

Step 3: Evaluate the truth value of individual statement \( q \) and its negation \( \sim q \).
Vertical angles are nonadjacent angles formed by two intersecting lines. Since \( \angle {ptA}{ptB}{ptC} \) and \( \angle {ptC}{ptB}{ptD} \) share a common side ray \( \overrightarrow{{ptB}{ptC}} \), they are adjacent angles and cannot be vertical. Therefore, statement \( q \) is false, making its negation \( \sim q \) TRUE.

Step 4: Evaluate the complete conjunction \( \sim p \wedge \sim q \).
A conjunction ("and" statement) is true if and only if both of its components evaluate to true:
\[ \text{True} \wedge \text{True} = \text{TRUE} \]
This balances out to a final value of TRUE.

Conclusion Summary:
• Compound Statement: \( \angle {ptA}{ptB}{ptC} \) and \( \angle {ptC}{ptB}{ptD} \) are not complementary, and \( \angle {ptA}{ptB}{ptC} \) and \( \angle {ptC}{ptB}{ptD} \) are not vertical angles.
• Truth Value: TRUE

3 Logical Arguments and Line Relationshi.question:
Sketch a geometric diagram according to the following: Points {ptA}, {ptB}, and {ptD} form a straight angle line with \( \overrightarrow{{ptB}{ptC}} \) extending upward:



Statements:
\( p \): \( \angle {ptA}{ptB}{ptC} \) and \( \angle {ptC}{ptB}{ptD} \) are complementary.
\( q \): \( \angle {ptA}{ptB}{ptC} \) and \( \angle {ptC}{ptB}{ptD} \) are vertical angles.
\( r \): \( \overline{{ptA}{ptB}} \cong \overline{{ptB}{ptD}} \)

Write out the compound statement for the disjunction \( p \vee \sim r \) in words, determine its final truth value, and explain your reasoning fully.
3 Logical Arguments and Line Relationshi.answer:
Here is the complete logical breakdown and step-by-step evaluation for the compound logic statement:

Step 1: Write the compound statement in words.
The symbol \( \sim \) represents a negation ("not"), and the symbol \( \vee \) represents a disjunction ("or"). Translating \( p \vee \sim r \) gives:
"\( \angle {ptA}{ptB}{ptC} \) and \( \angle {ptC}{ptB}{ptD} \) are complementary, OR segment \( \overline{{ptA}{ptB}} \) is not congruent to segment \( \overline{{ptB}{ptD}} \)."

Step 2: Evaluate the truth value of individual statement \( p \).
Complementary angles must add up to exactly \( 90^\circ \). Because points \( {ptA} \), \( {ptB} \), and \( {ptD} \) lie along a straight horizontal baseline frame, they form a straight angle. By the Linear Pair Postulate, \( \angle {ptA}{ptB}{ptC} \) and \( \angle {ptC}{ptB}{ptD} \) are supplementary and must add up to exactly \( 180^\circ \). Therefore, statement \( p \) is FALSE.

Step 3: Evaluate the truth value of individual statement \( r \) and its negation \( \sim r \).
Looking at the diagram blueprint, there are no geometry indicators or tick marks stating that vertex point \( {ptB} \) is the exact numerical midpoint of the horizontal line segment. Therefore, we cannot assume segment lengths match, meaning statement \( r \) is fundamentally false. Negating a false statement makes it true, so \( \sim r \) is TRUE (it is true that they are not confirmed congruent).

Step 4: Evaluate the complete disjunction \( p \vee \sim r \).
A disjunction ("or" statement) is true if at least one of its components evaluates to true:
\[ \text{False} \vee \text{True} = \text{TRUE} \]
This balances out to a final value of TRUE.

Conclusion Summary:
• Compound Statement: \( \angle {ptA}{ptB}{ptC} \) and \( \angle {ptC}{ptB}{ptD} \) are complementary, or segment \( \overline{{ptA}{ptB}} \) is not congruent to segment \( \overline{{ptB}{ptD}} \).
• Truth Value: TRUE

CONSTRUCTION  {builder_name} is building a wooden gate following this diagram.



If \( m\angle LMN = {deg_given}^\circ \) and \( \angle LMN \cong \angle OMP \), what is \( m\angle NMP \)?

? {choice_A}
? {choice_B}
? {choice_C}
? {choice_D}
3 Logical Arguments and Line Relationshi.answer:
Here is the step-by-step geometric calculation to find the missing angle:

Step 1: Determine the measure of the congruent angle.
We are given that \( \angle LMN \cong \angle OMP \). Since congruent angles have completely identical measures:
\[ m\angle OMP = m\angle LMN = {deg_given}^\circ \]

Step 2: Use the straight angle relationship along the frame.
Points \( L \), \( M \), and \( O \) run straight across the bottom beam of the gate frame. This forms a straight line angle measuring exactly \( 180^\circ \). By the Angle Addition Postulate, the three contiguous component angles must add up to the total line measure:
\[ m\angle LMN + m\angle NMP + m\angle OMP = 180^\circ \]

Step 3: Substitute the known values and solve.
\[ {deg_given}^\circ + m\angle NMP + {deg_given}^\circ = 180^\circ \]
\[ {formula: 2 * deg_given}^\circ + m\angle NMP = 180^\circ \]
\[ m\angle NMP = 180^\circ - {formula: 2 * deg_given}^\circ = {correct_ans}^\circ \]

Therefore, the correct choice is {correct_letter}.

3 Logical Arguments and Line Relationshi.question:
WINDOWS  A contemporary architectural window is designed in the shape of a right trapezoid as shown below.



If the acute angle measures {deg_acute}°, what is the measure of the upper obtuse angle?

? {choice_A}
? {choice_B}
? {choice_C}
? {choice_D}
3 Logical Arguments and Line Relationshi.answer:
Here is the step-by-step geometric calculation to determine the missing angle measure:

Step 1: Identify the parallel lines in the window frame.
Because the window is a right trapezoid, the horizontal top frame edge and the horizontal bottom frame sill are perfectly parallel to each other.

Step 2: Apply consecutive interior angle properties.
When a slanting transversal line crosses two parallel lines, the consecutive interior angles formed (the acute angle and the obtuse angle) are **supplementary**. This means they always add up to exactly \( 180^\circ \):
\[ \text{Acute Angle} + \text{Obtuse Angle} = 180^\circ \]

Step 3: Substitute the known value and subtract.
\[ {deg_acute}^\circ + \text{Obtuse Angle} = 180^\circ \]
\[ \text{Obtuse Angle} = 180^\circ - {deg_acute}^\circ = {deg_obtuse}^\circ \]

Therefore, the correct choice is {correct_letter}.

3 Logical Arguments and Line Relationshi.question: Graph the line parallel to \( {orig_eq} \) that passes through the point \( ({x1}, {y1}) \).
3 Logical Arguments and Line Relationshi.answer:
Here is the step-by-step mathematical method to determine the equation and plot the parallel line:

Step 2: Find the parallel slope.
Parallel lines have slopes that are completely identical because they run in the exact same direction. Therefore, the slope of our new line is:
\[ m_2 = {m_val} \]

Step 3: Write the equation of the new line.
Using the point-slope formula \( y - y_1 = m(x - x_1) \) with our target point \( ({x1}, {y1}) \) and the parallel slope \( m_2 = {m_val} \):
\[ y - ({y1}) = {m_val}(x - ({x1})) \]
\[ y - {y1} = {m_val}(x - {x1}) \]
Converting this directly into slope-intercept form gives:
\[ y = {m_val}x + {b_para} \]

Step 4: Plot the line on the grid.
  • Start by placing a point directly at the given coordinate \( ({x1}, {y1}) \).
  • Use the parallel slope fraction \( {m_val} \) (rise over run) to navigate to the next coordinate points.
  • Draw a straight line completely through these points to finish the graph. This line will run perfectly alongside the original line without ever intersecting it.

3 Logical Arguments and Line Relationshi.question: Graph the line perpendicular to \( {orig_eq} \) that passes through the point \( ({x1}, {y1}) \).
3 Logical Arguments and Line Relationshi.answer:
Here is the step-by-step mathematical method to determine the equation and plot the perpendicular line:

Step 1: Identify the slope of the original line.
The given line is written in slope-intercept form \( y = mx + b \), where the original slope is:
\[ m_1 = {m_orig} \]

Step 2: Find the perpendicular slope.
Perpendicular lines have slopes that are negative reciprocals of one another (their product equals \(-1\)). Flip the fraction and change the algebraic sign:
\[ m_2 = {m_perp} \]

Step 3: Write the equation of the new line.
Using the point-slope formula \( y - y_1 = m(x - x_1) \) with our target point \( ({x1}, {y1}) \) and perpendicular slope \( m_2 = {m_perp} \):
\[ y - ({y1}) = {m_perp}(x - ({x1})) \]
\[ y - {y1} = {m_perp}(x - {x1}) \]
Converting this directly into slope-intercept form gives:
\[ y = {m_perp}x + {b_perp} \]

Step 4: Plot the line on the grid.
  • Start by placing a point directly at the given coordinate \( ({x1}, {y1}) \).
  • Use the perpendicular slope fraction \( {m_perp} \) (rise over run) to navigate to the next coordinate points.
  • Draw a straight line completely through these points to finish the graph.
